raw: As a disease that seriously affects the health of men and women of childbearing age, the incidence of infertility is increasing worldwide, and the popularization of assisted reproductive technology (ART) is expected to improve the situation.
However, invitro fertilization and embryo transfer (IVF) success rates are only about 50%, and IVF success rates are affected by a number of factors.
Despite four decades of refinement, in vitro fertilisation live birth rates plateau at 25-30% globally, largely due to limitations in subjective embryo selection.
STUDY QUESTION: Can artificial intelligence algorithms improve embryo selection in assisted reproduction?
WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY: Morphological assessment of embryos remains subjective with high inter-observer variability.
PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS, SETTING AND METHODS: Retrospective multicenter cohort of 1,200 IVF cycles.
MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: AI prediction achieved AUC 0.79 (95% CI 0.71–0.86) for clinical pregnancy.
LIMITATIONS, REASONS FOR CAUTION: The study was retrospective and requires prospective validation.
WIDER IMPLICATIONS OF THE FINDINGS: Standardized external benchmarks are warranted prior to clinical deployment.

Clinical pregnancy rates were significantly higher in the AI-assisted group (45.7%, 268/587) compared to the conventional group (38.1%, 223/585), with an adjusted odds ratio of 1.40 (95% confidence interval, 1.11-1.77; p = 0.004).
Metformin in gestational diabetes demonstrated comparable glycemic control with reduced maternal gestational weight gain compared with insulin.
At 2-year follow-up, offspring exposed to metformin demonstrated no adverse neurodevelopmental delays compared with insulin-exposed controls.
Robotic-assisted excision demonstrated lower operative blood loss with longer operating times but comparable 12-month pain reduction scores.
Spontaneous pregnancy rates at 18 months post-surgery were 42.1% following complete robotic resection of deep infiltrating nodules.
This review summarizes recent clinical evidence and ethical challenges of artificial intelligence in assisted reproduction.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the role of artificial intelligence and machine learning in assisted reproductive technologies.
METHODS: We searched PubMed and Scopus for studies evaluating machine learning algorithms in IVF.
RESULTS: Deep learning models improved blastocyst grading reproducibility across participating clinics.
CONCLUSIONS: Prospective randomized trials are required to confirm clinical benefit over standard morphology.
LIMITATIONS: Small sample size and retrospective single-center design limit generalizability.
A total of 420 patients were enrolled in this observational cohort between 2020 and 2023.
In conclusion, our findings suggest that AI-assisted time-lapse selection requires prospective validation before routine use.
